title: Model Catalog Demo - CascadeHealth
next_steps: Maya to send pricing and security pack
SE to run custom benchmark on CascadeHealth test corpus
action_items: Maya Patel | Send pricing + SOC2/ISO pack | 2026-12-02
Carlos Ramos | Run 3-model perf bench on 512/2048 seqs (A100/H100) | 2026-12-04

summary: Redwood AE/SE walked CascadeHealth through the Model Catalog UI, compatibility matrix and benchmark results. Main asks: predictable latency for 512/2048 seqs, private deployment options (VPC), SOC2/ISO docs, and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: pricing + security docs, SE benchmarks, and pilot kickoff next week.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 15:00 UTC | Duration ~46m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (SE), Dr. Leah Kim (CTO), Samir (ML), Nina (Dev Lead), Oliver (Procurement)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood Inference. Carlos and Jamie are with me today, we'll run through the model catalog and how you can pick open models, look at benchmarks and the compatibility matrix, and then show the console Optimize suggestions.

00:18 Dr. Leah: thanks, Maya. quick context: we're building an internal clinical notes assistant, must be HIPAA compliant, low p95 latency for 512 tokens, sometimes 2k sequences for summarization. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private.

00:34 Carlos: got it. quick clarification, when you say 2k seqs is that 2,048 tokens or like 3k?

00:38 Dr. Leah: yeah 2,048 typical, but we have outliers up to 3k.

00:45 Maya: perfect. we'll show filters in the model catalog for sequence-length profile, quantization compatibility, and also a hardware compat matrix that maps models to recommended instance types like A100, H100, and CPU fallbacks.

01:05 Samir: also curious about accuracy drop with int8 vs int4 quant, and whether Redwood provides verified perf/quality deltas.

01:12 Carlos: good question. in the catalog each model card includes a benchmarks tab: p50/p90/p95 latency traces, throughput tokens/sec, and a small quality delta report vs the FP16 baseline for common evals. there are caveats, some auto-transcribed words here: our quantization pipelines are test, um, are model-dependent — so int4 is available for a growing set, but Llama 2 70B int4 might show some degraded refusals on safety prompts, so we call that out.

01:40 Jamie: we also have a compatibility matrix: rows are models, columns are runtime features (kv cache, continuous batching, tensor cores, fused attention), and then per-hardware recommended kernels. you can export it as CSV.

01:58 Nina: can you show the UI?

02:02 Carlos: sure, sharing screen now — uh, gimme a sec, sorry screen perm — (screen share noise)

02:18 Carlos: okay on the left is filters: task (chat, completion, embeddings, rerank), model family, open vs curated, size buckets, supported quant formats. i'm typing "summarization" + seq-length filter -> choose 2048+. It highlights Mistral-8x7B, Llama-2-13B, Llama-2-70B, Falcon-40B in our catalog.

03:05 Dr. Leah: curious why Mistral shows much lower cost but similar qual in your bench?

03:12 Carlos: right — Mistral variants are compute-efficient for short-medium sequences, and our bench shows p95 latency lower on A100 for 512 seqs; however at 2048 the inference kernel behavior shifts and larger models can be more stable. the compatibility matrix flags that Mistral-8x7B has limited kv cache optimizations for very long context — we surfaced that in the "long context" column.

03:42 Samir: can you speak to the bench setup — synthetic tokens or real prompts? we need to know if numbers will translate to our clinical templates.

03:50 Carlos: we run both synthetic and corpus-based benches; the public model catalog shows synthetic median numbers and a small set of reference corpora (news, s2, user prompts). for enterprise pilots we run a custom bench on your corpus and produce a CSV with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and memory footprint per request.

04:12 Maya: i'll put that in the next steps — custom bench from Carlos. also we'll include the perf spreadsheet and kernel notes.

04:20 Dr. Leah: privacy question — hosted vs private: if we go hosted, how is PHI protected?

04:26 Maya: hosted has encryption at rest and in transit, SOC2, contract terms about data retention — but for PHI we usually recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) so data never leaves your network and you can use KMS/HSM. i'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs.

04:44 Oliver: procurement will need pricing for both hosted and dedicated commits, and a pilot pricing option.

04:50 Maya: yep, pricing sheet will include pay-as-you-go hosted, reserved capacity for Dedicated, and an estimate for Private deployment.

05:00 Carlos: back to the catalog — here's the model card for Llama-2-70B: top shows architecture, tokenizer, supported sequence lengths, and then a compatibility matrix tile. it lists supported quant formats (FP16, int8, int4 experimental), recommended kernels for H100/A100, and estimated vram at 512/2048. see column "kv cache compatible" — yes for 70B on our runtime we keep KV memory efficient.

05:36 Samir: that vram estimate — is it with continuous batching on?

05:39 Carlos: the vram numbers assume single-request no batch; we surface alternate tables for batch sizes 4/8/16. continuous batching can reduce effective memory pressure if requests share prefixes, but that depends on your usage pattern.

06:00 Nina: what's the process for adding a custom model or a fine-tuned variant to the catalog?

06:05 Carlos: for Private/Dedicated you can bring-your-own model (BYOM) — we have onboarding scripts and a model validation pipeline that runs a small suite to build kernels, quantize, and populate the compatibility matrix. for hosted we can evaluate and onboard as part of an enterprise contract.

06:22 Dr. Leah: we have a fine-tuned BioBERT-based LLM for de-id and summarization — would that be supported?

06:28 Carlos: yes, as long as the architecture is supported by our runtime (transformer-based, standard attention). we'll run kernel selection and tell you if any ops are unsupported. note: custom tokenizers sometimes trip the batching heuristics — we test that in the onboarding run.

06:45 Speaker 3: um hm, slight background noise.

06:50 Maya: moving on to benchmarks — here's a sample benchmark sheet in the catalog. column headers: model, hw, seq, batch, p50_ms, p95_ms, throughput_tok_per_s, mem_gb. for example Llama-2-70B on H100: 512 seq p50 ~120ms p95 ~240ms throughput 1800 tok/s; at 2048 p50 ~480ms p95 ~920ms. these are ballpark — your results may vary.

07:25 Samir: those 2048 numbers look high for us — we need p95 < 600ms for 2k seqs in the critical path. can you hit that?

07:33 Carlos: depends on model and kernel. we can try a few options: 1) use a larger model with optimized kernels (70B on H100), 2) enable quant int8/4 with recompute quality checks, 3) use Dedicated reserved capacity to avoid noisy neighbors and get consistent latency. the compatibility matrix will indicate which models have low-latency kernels at 2k.

08:00 Dr. Leah: can Redwood route requests to cheaper models for low-risk queries and heavier models for sensitive ones? we want to balance cost.

08:09 Maya: yes, smart routing can be configured by policy: based on route, user role, or confidence. you can set fallback to a cheaper model, or run a re-rank step. in the console Optimize view we also surface cost per 1k tokens for each model and the expected latency.

08:30 Oliver: on SLAs, what uptime and latency SLOs do you include for Dedicated?

08:36 Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime 99.9% and latency targets per model tier; these are in the enterprise addendum. private deployments have separate support contracts.

08:46 Samir: second technical thing: how do you measure quality delta for quantization in the catalog? is it cross-entropy or human eval?

08:55 Carlos: a mix: we run automatic metrics (perplexity, Rouge, BLEU where applicable), unit tests for safety, and a small human-in-the-loop spot check for sensitive domains. for your pilot we'll do a domain-specific eval.

09:12 Dr. Leah: show me a compatibility matrix row for Mistral vs Llama-2 vs Falcon.

09:18 Carlos: ok pulling up the CSV — Mistral-8x7B: kernels: optimized for A100 tensor cores, kv cache: partial, quant: int8 supported, int4 experimental, long context: limited. Llama-2-70B: kernels: fused attention on H100/A100, kv cache: efficient, quant: int8/int4 available with small qual delta for summarization. Falcon-40B: kernels tuned for high throughput on H100, memory footprint high but strong long-context perf.

09:58 Nina: how do I interpret the "kv cache partial" cell?

10:01 Carlos: it means our runtime stores some of the cache on-device but falls back to host memory for very long contexts which impacts p95. we'll include an explanation in the CSV export.

10:14 Dr. Leah: any security caveats with custom kernels? we need code-auditability.

10:19 Maya: for Private deployments you get the runtime image and signing options, and we can run audits on request. for hosted we provide attestations and runtime logs with trace IDs. we also integrate with your KMS for key control.

10:35 Samir: can we see the Optimize suggestions now?

10:38 Carlos: yep open the Optimize tab — top shows "suggested batching" and "quantization profile". for your pattern (many 512, some 2k) it suggests: keep 512 requests on Mistral or Llama-13B for low-cost fast responses, route 2k summarization to Llama-70B on H100 with int8, and enable prefix caching for repeat patterns. estimated cost reduction ~22% vs naively using 70B for everything.

11:10 Dr. Leah: that sounds promising. what is prefix caching?

11:13 Carlos: prefix/KV caching keeps previously computed KV states for shared prefixes so subsequent requests that share the beginning of a conversation are much faster; effective for chat flows or templated inputs.

11:25 Samir: any limitations for PHI? does prefix caching store identifiable info?

11:29 Maya: caching respects retention policies and can be disabled; for PHI we generally recommend disabling cross-session cache and retaining only per-request ephemeral state unless you have strict controls. we'll document storage TTLs in the security pack.

11:45 Nina: can I get the model cards as JSON so I can programmatically filter?

11:49 Carlos: yes, model catalog exposes an API (catalog.models.list) that returns model metadata and the compatibility matrix; we also return benchmark CSV links. we'll include API keys and a quickstart in the pilot repo.

12:03 Dr. Leah: about costs — can you show an example cost per 1k tokens for a routed flow?

12:08 Carlos: in the Optimize view we show cost per 1k tokens aggregated by model and by route, and also simulated monthly spend based on traffic. example: Llama-13B hosted ~ $0.09 / 1k tokens, Mistral-8x7B ~ $0.05 / 1k, Llama-70B ~ $0.45 / 1k (these are illustrative). We'll provide specific numbers in the pricing sheet.

12:38 Oliver: procurement needs the pilot SOW and acceptance criteria for the POC.

12:45 Maya: we'll draft SOW: 2-week pilot, 50k tokens/day, custom benchmarks, success metric p95 <600ms for 2k requests (for non-critical path we can accept higher) and quality above threshold on your eval set.

13:02 Samir: if we do Dedicated, how do rollouts work — can we canary new model versions?

13:07 Carlos: yes, console supports canary rollouts, traffic split, automatic rollback based on perf or quality regression. you can pin model versions per route.

13:20 Dr. Leah: last Q: are there pre-built evaluation harnesses for clinical tasks?

13:24 Jamie: we have a reference eval suite with templates for summarization, de-identification checks, and safety tests; for enterprise we'll build a custom harness using your gold set.

13:35 Maya: quick recap and next steps: 1) Maya sends pricing + SOC2/ISO + console quickstart (Maya) 2) Carlos runs custom bench on A100/H100 for 512 and 2048 seq using your sample prompts (Carlos) 3) Nina shares sample prompts + success criteria (Nina) 4) schedule pilot kickoff for week of Dec 7 (all)

13:58 Dr. Leah: sounds good. one note: we might need a private deployment evaluation — can you include on-prem checklist?

14:05 Maya: yes, that's in the security pack; i'll add on-prem checklist and typical infra specs.

14:12 Oliver: ok procurement will wait for SOW and pricing.

14:18 Maya: thanks everyone for your time. we'll follow up with the docs and bench results.

14:22 Speaker 2: thanks, bye.

-- End of transcript --
